items.title: [Bug]: PR #51726's >=160GiB tier captures MI300X (191.98 GiB), doubling max_num_batched_tokens and breaking KV cache init for DeepSeek-V4-Pro at 1M
items.body:
### Your current environment

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

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Summary

#51726 added a device_memory >= 160 * GiB_bytes tier setting OPENAI_API_SERVER: 16384 (from 8192), commented as targeting B200/B300. The branch gates on raw capacity, so MI300X (191.98 GiB) also falls into it. The default silently doubles, peak activation during profile_run() doubles with it, and DeepSeek-V4-Pro can no longer initialize its KV cache at 1M context.
```
  -if device_memory >= 70 * GiB_bytes and "a100" not in device_name:
  -    # For GPUs like H100 and MI300x, use larger default values.
  +if device_memory >= 160 * GiB_bytes:
  +    # for GPUs like B200/B300 with >= 160GB memory, use the largest defaults
```
The replaced comment named MI300x explicitly on the 70 GiB branch.

The threshold doesn't separate the devices it names: B200 ≈ 192 GB ≈ MI300X; only B300 is 288 GB. Any 192 GB-class GPU now inherits a 288 GB-class default.

Repro
```
  VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 \
  vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro --dtype auto -tp 8 \
    --load-format dummy --no-enable-prefix-caching --kv-cache-dtype fp8
```

  ValueError: To serve at least one request with the model's max seq len (1048576),
  23.32 GiB KV cache is needed, which is larger than the available KV cache memory (13.41 GiB).

Measured

8×MI300X, TP8, fp8 KV, dummy weights. max_model_len = 1,048,576 and requirement = 23.32 GiB in every row; only the supply side moves.

  ┌────────────────────────┬─────────────────┬──────────────┬────────┐
  │ max_num_batched_tokens │ peak activation │ KV available │ result │
  ├────────────────────────┼─────────────────┼──────────────┼────────┤
  │ 4096                   │ 5.57 GiB        │ 30.07 GiB    │ OK     │
  ├────────────────────────┼─────────────────┼──────────────┼────────┤
  │ 8192 (pre-#51726)      │ 11.14 GiB       │ 24.55 GiB    │ OK     │
  ├────────────────────────┼─────────────────┼──────────────┼────────┤
  │ 16384 (post-#51726)    │ 22.28 GiB       │ 13.41 GiB    │ FAIL   │
  └────────────────────────┴─────────────────┴──────────────┴────────┘

Activation is linear at ~1.393 MB/token; +8192 tokens costs ~11.1 GiB. I derived this from the 8192/16384 pair, predicted 4096 → 30.12 GiB, and measured 30.07 GiB (0.2% error).

  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.97 still fails (23.01 GiB) — utilization cannot recover 11 GiB.

Why this model is exposed: MLA replicates latent KV on every rank (num_key_value_heads: 1), so TP8 gives 8× weights but 1× KV. Weights consume 149.56 GiB/GPU, leaving only 24.25 GiB. Max concurrency at 1M was already just 1.67×. Control: Qwen2.5-72B (GQA) on the same image at 16384 gets 155.5 GiB KV and starts fine — the regression needs both MLA replication and a large-MoE weight footprint.

Env

vllm 0.26.1rc1.dev1187+g1900d481f, torch 2.12.0+rocm7.14.0, triton 3.7.1, aiter 0.1.19, 8×MI300X (gfx942), ROCm 7.14, rocm/vllm-dev:torch212-py312-cdna-prebuild-triton. Regression window: v0.27.1 passes (Aug 13); #51726 merged Aug 11.

Asks

1. Should the tier gate on vendor/arch rather than raw capacity?
2. @yewentao256 — do you see the same KV-init failure serving DeepSeek-V4-Pro at 1M on B200 post-#51726? Given #51454 reports V4-Pro at only ~2.0× concurrency on 8×B200 under TP8 (same MLA replication), B200 looks similarly tight — so this may not be ROCm-specific.

Prior art: #51454, #43753.

Filed with AI assistance (Claude Code); all measurements independently reproduced on hardware.

items.title: [Bug]: VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD deadlocks at kernel warmup on single GPU (TP=1) - Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on GB10/sm_121
items.body:
### Summary

Serving `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` with `VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD=1` at `tensor_parallel_size=1` hangs permanently during startup. Engine init completes fully — weights load, KV cache is allocated, FlashInfer autotune finishes — and then the process goes silent before `init engine took Xs`. The API server never starts. No exception, no CUDA OOM, no kernel OOM-kill.

Reproduced 3/3 times, waiting 25, 60 and 60 minutes.

Full py-spy dump and container log (secrets redacted): https://gist.github.com/jdmays13/8b081bffc59d270d3125e6eac521f207

### Environment

- vLLM `v0.1.dev20073+g8e685d198`, image `vllm/vllm-openai:qwen38-flash-next`
- NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark), `sm_121`, aarch64, driver 580.142, 128 GB unified memory
- Model: `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` (135.2 GB on disk), `quantization=modelopt_fp4`
- `tensor_parallel_size=1`, `max_model_len=32768`, `speculative_config={"method":"mtp","num_spec_tokens":4}`
- `VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD=1`

### Last log lines before the silence

```
[model_runner.py:407] Model loading took 80.28 GiB memory and 654.015720 seconds
[connector.py:231] PleOffload: registered 1 PleOffloadLayer(s) (dp_rank=0, tp_rank=0, ipc_addr=ipc:///tmp/ea99706f-...)
[kv_cache_utils.py:2258] GPU KV cache size: 271,610 tokens, Maximum concurrency for 32,768 tokens per request: 8.29x
[autotuner.py:852] flashinfer.jit: [Autotuner]: Autotuning process ends
[gpu_worker.py:919] Free memory on device (115.55/121.63 GiB) on startup
```

Then nothing for 46 minutes, until we killed it.

### py-spy: the deadlock

Main thread is blocked in the warmup forward pass:

```
Thread 365 (active): "MainThread"
    replay (torch/cuda/graphs.py:186)
    __call__ (vllm/compilation/cuda_graph.py:360)
    warmup_kernels (vllm/v1/worker/gpu/warmup.py:330)
        batch_req_state: (["_warmup_0_", "_warmup_1_", ...])
```

The PLE offload worker is blocked waiting for a request that never arrives:

```
Thread 532 (idle): "ple-offload-dp0"
    wait (threading.py:355)
        timeout: None
    get (queue.py:171)
        block: True
        timeout: None
    _request_loop (vllm/v1/ple_offload/connector.py:263)
        self: <PleOffloadConnector at 0x...>
        ipc_addr: "ipc:///tmp/1bcc22d1-..."
        socket: <Socket at 0x...>
        request: <PleOffloadRequest at 0x...>
```

The warmup forward needs n-gram/PLE rows to make progress. The worker that would supply them is parked in `Queue.get(block=True, timeout=None)`. Neither side advances, and because both waits are untimed there is no failure — just an indefinite hang that is indistinguishable from a slow load.

### `--enforce-eager` does not help

With `enforce_eager=True` (confirmed in the logged engine config) CUDA graph capture is skipped entirely, and startup still hangs at the same point with the same silence. So this is not specific to graph replay — removing graphs only changes where the main thread waits, not that it waits.

### The offload itself works

Worth stating, since it isolates the bug to readiness rather than to the feature: resident memory is **80.28 GiB** for a 135.2 GB checkpoint. The ~51.2 GB n-gram table (`ngram_vocab_size_base=20000000` × `ple_embed_dim=2560`) is genuinely kept out of device memory, which is exactly what the flag promises and is what makes this model viable on a 128 GB box at all. It simply never becomes ready to serve.

### Possibly relevant

The documented PLE-offload example uses `--tensor-parallel-size 4`, and the validated recipes are TP2/TP4 on GB300, so TP=1 may be an untested path. #51340 reports a superficially similar warmup hang from missing inter-rank synchronization, though that one is multi-node. #53908 requests auxiliary-GPU offloading for these same embeddings — related feature, different target.

Happy to run further diagnostics on this hardware if it would help; the box is available and reproducing takes about 15 minutes.

items.title: [Bug]: GLM-5.3-Flash on ROCm (gfx950): SparseAttnIndexerKpool.forward_hip() missing gate_score — platform guard hides a fixable gap
items.body:
### Your current environment

```
Hardware   : 8x AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950)
ROCm       : 7.2.3
torch      : 2.12.0
vLLM       : 0.26.1rc1.dev716+g933876c38.rocm723
             (built from PR #53906 "add GLM-5.3-Flash support", VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=rocm,
              PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx950)
Model      : local snapshot of zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash (FP8, 62 safetensors)
```

### 🐛 Describe the bug

We built PR #53906 for ROCm to see where AMD support for GLM-5.3-Flash actually stands. Summary: **the platform guard is not the real blocker — a stale `forward_hip()` is.** Sharing the details in case they save someone a cycle.

#### 1. The build itself is clean

`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=rocm` with `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx950` completes with `rc=0`. Both `Glm5NextForCausalLM` and `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` register, and `current_platform` reports `rocm`.

#### 2. The guard rejects ROCm at import time

`vllm/models/glm5next/__init__.py`:

```python
if current_platform.is_rocm() or current_platform.is_xpu():
    raise NotImplementedError(
        "GLM-5.3-Flash currently supports NVIDIA SM90 and above only.")
```

This fires before any model code executes. Worth noting what sits underneath it: grepping `vllm/models/glm5next/` for `flashinfer|tilelang|trtllm|flashmla` returns **zero** hits, and the only kernels there are `@triton.jit` (`ops/fused_eh_norm.py`, `ops/kpool_compress.py`). So the guard looks precautionary rather than load-bearing.

#### 3. With the guard removed, weight loading succeeds

```
INFO [default_loader.py:430] Loading weights took 61.57 seconds
```

Served with `--tensor-parallel-size 8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 131072 --max-num-seqs 64 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --trust-remote-code`.

#### 4. The actual blocker

```
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error
'SparseAttnIndexerKpool.forward_hip() got an unexpected keyword argument 'gate_score''
```

In `vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer_kpool.py` the three dispatch paths have diverged:

```python
def forward_native(self, hidden_states, q_quant, k, weights, *, ...)   # keyword-only args incl. gate_score
def forward_cuda(self,   hidden_states, q_quant, k, weights, *, ...)   # keyword-only args incl. gate_score
def forward_hip(self,    hidden_states, q_quant, k, weights):          # stops at weights
```

`forward_hip` is not a stub — it dispatches to `torch.ops.vllm.rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer`. It simply predates this PR's indexer changes. It also still carries:

```python
assert not self.use_fp4_cache, "AMD platform doesn't support fp4 cache yet"
```

#### What this suggests

AMD enablement here looks less like "port the model" and more like "teach the existing AITER indexer path about `gate_score` / kpool". Whether that is a signature passthrough or genuine kernel work inside AITER is the part we cannot judge from the outside — that is really a question for whoever owns `rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer`.

We are happy to run diagnostics or test patches on this node; ROCm turnaround for us is quick.

items.title: [Bug]: M_LOG2E availability depends on build configuration in the FlashMLA extension
items.body:
### Your current environment

### Environment

- Windows Server 2025
- Visual Studio Build Tools with MSVC
- CUDA/NVCC 13.2
- Python 3.12
- PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130
- SystemPanic/vllm-windows 0.25-based deployment
- DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731
- 4 x H200 NVL GPUs

### 🐛 Describe the bug

### Background

I encountered this issue while building the vllm-project/FlashMLA fork through SystemPanic/vllm-windows for a deployment on H200 NVL GPUs.

### Problem

The vLLM-specific FlashMLA extension uses `M_LOG2E` in:

    csrc/extension/sm90/dense_fp8/softmax.h
    csrc/extension/sm90/dense_fp8/pybind.cpp

For example:

    const float max_scaled = max(mi) == -INFINITY ? 0.f
                             : max(mi) * (
                                   Scale_max ? scale : float(M_LOG2E));

`M_LOG2E` represents `log2(e)` and is commonly available in GNU/Linux build environments. Its availability is nevertheless implementation-specific.

With MSVC, the `M_*` constants are normally exposed only when `_USE_MATH_DEFINES` is defined before the relevant math header is included. The current source can therefore depend on build flags and translation-unit include order when compiled with NVCC and MSVC.

I understand that native Windows with NVCC and MSVC may not be part of the supported FlashMLA build matrix. However, removing this dependency would be a small cross-platform portability improvement and would not change the existing Linux result.

### Tested source-level fix

The FlashMLA extension built successfully after replacing `float(M_LOG2E)` with the equivalent float literal:

    - float(M_LOG2E)
    + 1.4426950408889634f

For the primary file, the tested change was:

    diff --git a/csrc/extension/sm90/dense_fp8/softmax.h b/csrc/extension/sm90/dense_fp8/softmax.h
    --- a/csrc/extension/sm90/dense_fp8/softmax.h
    +++ b/csrc/extension/sm90/dense_fp8/softmax.h
    @@
    -const float max_scaled = max(mi) == -INFINITY ? 0.f : max(mi) * (Scale_max ? scale : float(M_LOG2E));
    +const float max_scaled = max(mi) == -INFINITY ? 0.f : max(mi) * (Scale_max ? scale : 1.4426950408889634f);

The original expression explicitly converts `M_LOG2E` to a 32-bit `float`. The replacement literal is also a `float` because of the `f` suffix.

Both expressions round to the same IEEE-754 float32 value, so the tested change preserves the numerical result and does not alter the algorithm.

A project-owned named constant could avoid repeating the literal, for example:

    inline constexpr float kLog2E = 1.4426950408889634f;

### Alternative build-level workaround

The issue can also be avoided in the vLLM CMake integration by defining `_USE_MATH_DEFINES` for both FlashMLA extension targets:

    target_compile_definitions(
        _flashmla_C PRIVATE _USE_MATH_DEFINES=1
    )

    target_compile_definitions(
        _flashmla_extension_C PRIVATE _USE_MATH_DEFINES=1
    )

This is a smaller integration-specific workaround and keeps the existing source unchanged.

### Related shared-source occurrences

The same dependency on `M_LOG2E` also appears in source inherited from `deepseek-ai/FlashMLA`, including:

    csrc/api/dense_decode.h
    csrc/sm90/decode/dense/splitkv_mla.cuh
    csrc/sm90/decode/sparse_fp8/splitkv_mla.cuh
    csrc/smxx/decode/combine/combine.cu
    csrc/sm100/prefill/dense/kernel/sm100_fmha_bwd_kernel_tma_warpspecialized.hpp
    csrc/sm100/prefill/dense/kernel/sm100_fmha_bwd_mla_kernel_tma_warpspecialized.hpp

items.title: [Bug]: --cpu-offload-params cannot reach token embeddings built outside make_layers
items.body:
## Description

`--offload-backend uva --cpu-offload-params embed_tokens` is a useful
single-GPU deployment profile for models with a large, untied input embedding.
The table is accessed as a sparse row gather, so it can free several GiB for KV
cache without streaming a dense weight on every decode step.

Today the selector silently matches zero bytes for token embeddings created
outside `make_layers()`. `Qwen3_5TextModel.embed_tokens` is one concrete
example, but the reachability gap is in the common offloader path rather than
in Qwen quantization.

## Reproduction

Model: Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4, tensor parallel size 1, untied BF16 input embedding
`[248320, 5120]` and separate NVFP4 `lm_head`.

```text
--offload-backend uva
--cpu-offload-gb 2.5
--cpu-offload-params embed_tokens
```

On the unmodified 0.27.1/0.28.0 construction path, the offloader is enabled but
no embedding parameter is visited, so there is no `Total CPU offloaded
parameters` record and model residency is unchanged.

The reason is that `get_offloader().wrap_modules()` is called for the decoder
stack created by `make_layers()`. The token embedding is constructed directly
before that stack. The final merged form of PR #53120, commit
`61d4f56635e0f2faae4bd60e6da88a53c9d3affb`, adds prefix-aware routing for
multimodal towers through `SupportsMultiModal._mark_tower_model`; it does not
route token embeddings.

## Expected behavior

An explicitly selected token embedding should be reachable by the existing UVA
offloader, with its fully qualified prefix preserved for exact-segment
matching. At minimum, the initial supported scope can be:

- `tensor_parallel_size == 1`;
- an untied input embedding; and
- UVA available with pinned host memory.

Unsupported TP or tied-weight configurations should fail clearly when the
embedding selector is present. An unmatched selector should also warn instead
of silently reporting success with zero bytes.

A new checkpoint format is not necessary. The existing runtime arguments are
the right interface; only reachability and validation are missing. A dedicated
`--offload-embedding` convenience flag could be considered later, but would
duplicate `--cpu-offload-params embed_tokens` unless it adds the safety checks
above.

## Local prototype and completed measurement

A post-load common-loader hook, using the existing `UVAOffloader`, was tested
without changing any checkpoint byte. It runs after safetensors loading and
`process_weights_after_loading`, rejects tied weights and TP greater than one,
and matched only `language_model.model.embed_tokens`:

```text
Total CPU offloaded parameters: 2.37 GiB
Model loading:                  16.19 -> 13.82 GiB
FP8 KV cache:                 269,691 -> 327,147 tokens
```

The server used the original public three-shard Gittensor checkpoint, retained
the separate packed NVFP4 `lm_head`, and used no MTP or speculative decoding.
An in-process full-vocabulary gate executed the actual embedding module over
all 248,320 rows before and after offload. All 1,271,398,400 BF16 output
elements were bitwise equal, with identical SHA-256
`a158f24c6ad72736067768b4255e70a384e2e931f601b12f853e98ce83ec6bbe`.

A fresh-cache RTX 5090 A/B/B/A bracket sent 64 independent requests at every
C8/C12/C16/C20/C24/C32/C48/C64 point. Each request used about 15,000 input and
256 output tokens. Both resident runs admitted 17 simultaneous active
requests; both UVA runs admitted 21, a repeat-stable gain of four or 23.5%.
All runs had zero preemptions. Best clean output throughput was
174.16/174.49 tok/s resident and 173.44/173.63 tok/s UVA. Across identical
points, the conservative worst-UVA/best-resident ratio ranged from 98.34% to
99.58%.

The local all-purpose promotion gate remained closed because it required at
least 99% throughput at every point and non-inferior C20 tail latency. That
does not change the feature request: selective embedding reachability
reproducibly trades about 0.4% best-throughput and at most 1.7% at a shared
point for 23.5% more active long-context requests on this single-GPU profile.
The immutable comparison SHA-256 is
`1ea420133acf8593fc2793e540fdc24742d0439f043d42ae0efc9277fc7884db`.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used (Codex and Claude) in the investigation, prototype, measurements, and preparation of this issue. Measurements were executed on real hardware.

items.title: [RFC]: Native Text Watermarking Support
items.body:
### Motivation.

Text watermarking for LLMs is a process by which we perturb the output of a model in such a way that is detectable after generation. This process allows us to test whether a sequence of text is consistent with a watermarked generation process after the fact.

Watermarking is a necessary functionality in vLLM, because:
- It has become an important part of responsible LLM deployment
- It has become required by regulation by certain entities, to support provenance and transparency requirements (see EU AI Act, Article 50(2) and California SB 942)
- It is a modification of the sampling process, which cannot be modified by downstream consumers

### Proposed Change.

We propose the implementation of native vLLM watermarking during sampling, using techniques such as Gumbel-max or SynthID-Text.

#### Desiderata

1. Non-distortion - the watermark should not alter the expected output distribution of a model over keyed generations, nor rely on metadata attached to an output.
2. Detectable - the watermark should be reliably detectable using inexpensive techniques, to allow for large-scale scoring.

#### Proposed Algorithm

We propose an initial implementation using the Gumbel-max algorithm (Aaronson and Kirchner, 2023) which has multiple desirable qualities:
- Single-token (can be adjusted for single-sequence non-distortion) of the model's output distribution, see see G.3 of [SynthID-Text Appendix](https://media.springernature.com/original/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41586-024-08025-4/MediaObjects/41586_2024_8025_MOESM1_ESM.pdf)
- Fast, relative to other schemes
- Unintrusive to implement, as it does not require access to significant parts of a model or request state
- Good detectability, using inexpensive methods
- May be altered to support speculative sampling

This algorithm uses a pseudo-random function (PRF) to create a deterministic keyed vector of uniform-random values `r_k ~ U(0, 1)`. At each position, we them sample `argmax_x r_k(x) ^ 1/p(x)`. The Gumbel-max identity allows us to structure our sampling by a key `k` without changing the distribution `p`.

Given a sequence of text, we can then recalculate `r_k` for each token, and `score = sum_t -log(1-r_t)` over our sequence. Under the null, `S` follows `Gamma(n, 1)`, so we have a length-adjusted p-value: this can be used with a threshold to classify a sequence as watermarked.

#### Implementation

The implementation is divided into three independent components: generation, detection primitives, and an optional detection service.

##### Watermarked generation

The initial implementation will support Model Runner V2 and Gumbel-max watermarking. Speculative decoding is out of scope initially, but may be supported with dual-key approaches: see https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.12456 and https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.01428

Watermarking is configured at engine startup:

```python
@dataclass
class WatermarkConfig:
    algorithm: Literal["gumbel"]
    key: int
    context_width: int = 4
```

The sampling pipeline remains unchanged until final token selection:

```text
model logits
    |
existing penalties and constraints
    |
temperature, min-p, top-k and top-p
    |
final token selection
    |
watermark disabled → existing random sampler
watermark enabled  → configured Watermarker
```

A shared `Watermarker` interface will define the algorithm-specific final selection. The initial `GumbelWatermarker` replaces the ordinary random draw with the keyed Gumbel-max draw. Greedy requests remain ordinary greedy sampling, as they cannot be watermarked.

This isolates watermarking from the model runner and allows us to extend support to additional algorithms, such as SynthID-Text.

##### Detection primitives

Basic detection does not require model weights or inference (although more advanced techniques that do this may be considered). vLLM will expose reusable detector primitives that expect token IDs:

```python
detector = GumbelWatermarkDetector(
    key=key,
    context_width=context_width,
)

result = detector.detect(token_ids)
```

The result contains the aggregate score, p-value, number of scored tokens, and threshold-based classification.

Shared detector logic handles context construction, repeated-context deduplication (necessary for certain guarantees of non-distortion), score aggregation, and thresholding. Concrete implementations will provide the token-level scoring and the corresponding p-value if available, if not an aggregate score.

##### [OPTIONAL] Detection endpoint

vLLM could additionally provide a CPU-only service for searching across multiple tokenizers and watermark configurations:

```text
vllm launch watermark-detector --config detectors.yaml
```

This process loads tokenizers and detector configurations without needing to load any weights. Configurations can be expressed as explicit profiles:

```yaml
profiles:
  - id: mistral-watermark-2026-08
    tokenizer: mistralai/text-tokenizer-v1
    algorithm: gumbel
    key: 42
    context_width: 4
```

Each profile has the tokenizer, algorithm, key and additional parameters required to reproduce detection. This avoids applying incompatible combinations from independent lists of tokenizers and keys.

A detection request accepts text and optional profile or model hints to accelerate detection and improve scoring. Without hints, the service searches all configured profiles:

```text
text
    |
tokenize once per distinct tokenizer
    |
score against compatible detector profiles
    |
correct for the number of profiles searched
    |
return matching profiles and adjusted p-values
```

Searching multiple profiles increases the probability of a false positive, so we will therefore apply a Bonferroni correction:

```text
adjusted_p = min(1, number_of_profiles_searched × smallest_raw_p)
```

The response reports both raw and search-adjusted p-values, while classification uses the adjusted value.

The output of python collect_env.py ```text ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 Libc version : glibc-2.39 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.13.0+cu130 Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ROCM used to build PyTorch : N/A ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.3 (main, Jun 19 2026, 12:46:00) [GCC 13.3.0] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-6.8.0-1010-gcp-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True CUDA runtime version : 12.0.140 GPU models and configuration : GPU 0-7: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (single GPU used for this report, TP=1) Nvidia driver version : 580.173.02 ============================== CPU Info ============================== Architecture: x86_64 Model name: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Platinum 8481C CPU @ 2.70GHz CPU(s): 208 Hypervisor vendor: KVM ============================== vLLM Info ============================== vLLM Version : 0.28.0 vLLM Build Flags: CUDA Archs: Not Set; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled GPU Topology: NV18 all-to-all (8x H100 SXM), TP=1 used Relevant packages: vllm==0.28.0 torch==2.13.0 transformers==5.15.1 flashinfer-python==0.6.16.post3 compressed-tensors==0.17.0 xgrammar==0.2.3 ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug **Summary.** `--enable-prefix-caching` together with MTP speculative decoding still corrupts output on hybrid (GDN/Mamba) Qwen3.5-class models in **v0.28.0**. A small fraction of responses degenerate into repeated punctuation (`!!!!…`) or come back empty. This is the same failure as #43559, which was closed as completed on 2026-08-06 — the merged scheduler-side fix (#51113) does not cover it, and the cache-manager-side fixes (#43650, #48375) are still open. **Model.** Qwen3.5-architecture dense 27B VLM (`Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, hybrid: Gated DeltaNet linear-attention layers + full attention every 4th layer, vision tower), FP8 W8A8 compressed-tensors (`FP8_DYNAMIC`), with an MTP head present in the checkpoint (`Qwen3_5MTP` resolves at startup). TP=1, single H100. **Server command** (paths redacted): ```bash export VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS=1 export VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 vllm serve \ --served-model-name path-mini \ --port 8000 \ --max-model-len 62768 \ --max-num-seqs 32 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \ --enable-chunked-prefill \ --limit-mm-per-prompt.image 10 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --mamba-cache-mode align \ --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 2}' ``` Startup confirms the configuration: `Resolved architecture: Qwen3_5MTP`, `enable_prefix_caching=True`, `num_spec_tokens=2`, `GPU KV cache size: 576,637 tokens`, attention block size 800 (forced up to match the mamba page size), async scheduling enabled (default). **Workload.** Multi-step GUI-agent traces: each request is a conversation of prior steps plus 1–3 screenshots (sliding 2-image history), ~4k–12k prompt tokens, ~20–100 output tokens, `temperature=0`, client concurrency up to 32. Consecutive steps of the same episode share a long prefix, so prefix-cache hit rate climbs through a run. **Observed.** | vLLM | prefix caching | MTP | final prefix-cache hit rate | malformed responses | |---|---|---|---|---| | 0.26.0 | on | k=2 | 27.5% | 25 / 2,636 (0.95%) | | **0.28.0** | **on** | **k=2** | **31.7%** | **4 / 495 (0.81%)** | | 0.28.0 | on | k=2, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` | ~10% (see note) | 0 / 1,135 | Malformed = response is a run of repeated `!` characters, or empty content. `finish_reason` is normal; no HTTP 5xx, no crash, no traceback — the engine stays healthy and every other response in the same run is correct. Two observations that point at the prefix cache rather than at MTP alone: 1. **Rate tracks cache hit rate.** Corruption appears only once the prefix cache starts hitting, and scales with the hit rate. 2. **`--kv-cache-dtype fp8` appears to avoid it, but only by destroying the cache.** With fp8 KV, vLLM raises the attention block size 800 → 1600 (`platforms/interface.py`, so that one attention page covers one mamba page). Our requests share ~1,700 tokens of prefix, so at a 1600-token matching unit almost nothing is reusable: hit rate collapses from 31.7% to ~10%, and malformed responses go to 0/1,135. That is consistent with reduced exposure, not with fp8 fixing the underlying defect. (For the same reason `--block-size 800` cannot be used to compensate: the value is derived and only ever raised.) **Suspected cause** (already described in #43650 / #48375): `MambaManager.find_longest_cache_hit` in `vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py` accepts `drop_eagle_block` and never acts on it, so the final matched block — which can hold recurrent state written over draft positions that verification later rejected — stays reachable through the prefix cache and is reused by subsequent requests sharing that prefix. `FullAttentionManager` drops that block. In v0.28.0 the caller (`kv_cache_coordinator.py`) additionally skips the eagle margin for `MambaSpec` with the comment *"its finder never drops"*, i.e. caller and manager disagree about who is responsible. Applying **#43650** (6 lines, `max_num_blocks -= 1` when `use_eagle`) on top of v0.28.0 starts cleanly and shows no regression on an unrelated accuracy check (100 grounding requests at concurrency 32: 76% vs 75% unpatched, identical coordinate error, 0 malformed). Other users report it resolving the symptom outright (#43650: 18/39 → 39/39 on a private benchmark; `content: null` at ~1-in-8 fixed completely). **Expected.** `--enable-prefix-caching` + MTP on a hybrid Mamba/GDN model should be either correct or explicitly rejected at startup, not silently corrupting a fraction of responses. **Notes / questions** - Was #43559 closed by #51113 intentionally? #51113 fixes chunk alignment on the write path; the reports above (and this one) are about block dropping on the cache-read path, which neither #51113 nor #46384 appears to cover. - If #43650 is considered too blunt because a hybrid block can be 1k+ tokens, would a narrower fix be acceptable — e.g. dropping the trailing block only when that block actually contains unverified draft positions? - Happy to run any specific probe on this configuration; we can reproduce on demand with the workload above. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bug]: TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS in the environment is silently overwritten
items.body:
### Your current environment

Observed on `rocm/vllm:rocm7.14.0_rdna_ubuntu24.04_py3.14_pytorch_2.11.0_vllm_0.23.0` (vLLM 0.23.0); the line is unchanged on current `main` (`vllm/env_override.py`).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`vllm/env_override.py` sets `TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS` with a plain assignment on every `import vllm`:

```python
os.environ["TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS"] = "1"
```

so an explicit setting in the environment is silently ignored:

```
$ TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=8 python3 -c "import os, vllm.env_override; import torch._inductor.config as ic; print(os.environ['TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS'], ic.compile_threads)"
1 1
```

The default of 1 exists for good reasons (#10480, #10619) and this is not a request to change it. But there is currently no way to opt in to parallel Inductor compile short of patching the file, and the cost is real on multi-core hosts: compiling a 128-expert fused-MoE graph (`gemma-4-26B-A4B`) takes 26 minutes at one thread on an 8-core host, a 12B dense graph 24 minutes, with every core but one idle.

`os.environ.setdefault` keeps the default and lets a deliberate override through; with that one-line change the same command prints `8 8`, and with the variable unset it still prints `1 1`.

items.title: Sleep level=1 wake silently corrupts LoRA state (NemotronH NVFP4/Marlin, TP=2, WSL2): fixed-seed generation diverges after wake, adapter stops applying, no error raised
items.body:
## Environment

- vLLM 0.27.1, `vllm/vllm-openai` image digest `sha256:0a51ea5b4ae2dc5d81890e5173f54203d2a3ae0cfffe51b8fd2afd4391bfd967` (created 2026-08-11)
- Model: `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4` (`NemotronHForCausalLM`), served weight-only FP4 via the Marlin fallback on SM89
- `--tensor-parallel-size 2` on 2x RTX 4090, `--enable-lora --max-lora-rank 16 --lora-modules` (one adapter), `--enforce-eager --no-enable-prefix-caching --enable-sleep-mode`, `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1`
- Docker inside WSL2 (kernel 6.18.33.1, driver 610.88, Windows 11 26220). WSL2 may be load-bearing; happy to run diagnostics.

## What happens

Probe design: fixed-seed generation recorded before sleep, compared token-for-token after wake, with the adapter unchanged.

- `POST /sleep?level=1`: clean. `is_sleeping` reports true, VRAM actually frees (cards settle to 1.7GB + 0.9GB).
- `POST /wake_up`: the engine comes back answering, but corrupted. One GPU restores about 3GB lighter than its pre-sleep residency, the LoRA adapter silently stops applying (base and adapter routes return the same tokens), and both routes diverge from their own pre-sleep fixed-seed baselines. Both models answered questions that were not asked. No error, no log line, HTTP 200 throughout.

Level 2 behaves per its contract (discard weights, wake needs a re-push; wake without one generates from uninitialized weights). The bug report is level 1 only: state that claims to be restored, is not, and nothing fails loudly.

## Why it matters

Any adapter-swap RL loop or serve-train alternation that trusts level-1 sleep gets a silently wrong policy after the first cycle. Our workaround is a full engine stop/start between phases, which also makes the adapter swap a clean `--lora-modules` load. A wake that cannot restore state should fail loudly instead of serving corrupted weights.

## Repro sketch

1. Serve the NVFP4 checkpoint TP=2 with one LoRA adapter and sleep mode enabled.
2. Record fixed-seed completions for base and adapter routes.
3. `POST /sleep?level=1`, confirm `is_sleeping`, `POST /wake_up`.
4. Re-run the fixed-seed completions and compare bytes; check per-GPU residency against pre-sleep.

items.title: [Bug]: MTP draft allocates a second full vocab embedding, OOMing a 27B INT4 target that the baseline fits
items.body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment</summary>

```text
vLLM:     0.27.1 (pip, isolated venv)
torch:    2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0
GPU:      NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090, 24 GiB (23.56 GiB usable), sm_86
Driver:   610.43.02
OS:       Debian 13, kernel 6.12.101+deb13-amd64
Python:   3.13.5
Model:    RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-INT4 (compressed-tensors, ships model_mtp.safetensors)
          model_type qwen3_5, vocab_size 248320, hidden_size 5120,
          tie_word_embeddings false
```
</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Serving `RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-INT4` **without** speculative decoding works: the model loads,
`Available KV cache memory: 1.38 GiB`, `GPU KV cache size: 16,384 tokens`, and requests complete
normally. Adding `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'` fails during
weight loading, 0.12 GiB short:

```
ERROR ... [gpu_model_runner.py:5403] Failed to load model - not enough GPU memory.
torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.37 GiB.
GPU 0 has a total capacity of 23.56 GiB of which 2.25 GiB is free.
```

The 2.37 GiB request is a **second copy of the target's vocabulary embedding**.

#### Where it comes from

The failing allocation is not in a decoder layer:

```
vllm/model_executor/layers/vocab_parallel_embedding.py:325  __init__
vllm/model_executor/layers/vocab_parallel_embedding.py:50   create_weights
```

`vocab_parallel_embedding.py:50` is `UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod`, and the size matches exactly:

```
vocab_size 248320 x hidden_size 5120 x 2 bytes (bf16) = 2.37 GiB
```

`qwen3_5_mtp.py:82` builds that buffer unconditionally:

```python
self.embed_tokens = VocabParallelEmbedding(self.vocab_size, config.hidden_size)
```

But the checkpoint ships no MTP embedding. `model.safetensors.index.json` lists 15 MTP tensors --
`mtp.fc`, `mtp.layers.0.*`, `mtp.pre_fc_norm_embedding` -- and no `mtp.embed_tokens` or
`mtp.lm_head`. What fills the buffer is the **target's** embedding, remapped by the draft's own
loader (`qwen3_5_mtp.py:307`):

```python
elif any(key in name for key in ["embed_tokens", "lm_head"]):
    if "embed_tokens" in name:
        name = name.replace("language_model.", "")
```

So the draft shares the target's embedding in *weights* and duplicates it in *memory*: the same
2.37 GiB tensor is resident twice, and the copy is what pushes this configuration over the edge.

The same file already aliases in the other direction when the config allows it, so aliasing is an
expected pattern here rather than an exotic one:

```python
if config.tie_word_embeddings:
    self.lm_head = self.model.embed_tokens
```

`tie_word_embeddings` is `false` for this checkpoint, so that branch is not taken.

This is not specific to Qwen: `deepseek_mtp.py`, `mimo_mtp.py` and `qwen3_next_mtp.py` all build
`self.embed_tokens = VocabParallelEmbedding(...)` the same way. I have only measured the Qwen3.5
path.

#### Reproduce

```bash
# works
vllm serve RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-INT4 \
  --max-model-len 8192 --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-num-seqs 1 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 --no-enable-log-requests

# OOMs during weight loading
vllm serve RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-INT4 \
  --max-model-len 8192 --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-num-seqs 1 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 --no-enable-log-requests \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'
```

#### What I ruled out

Six attempts, and the "free" figure is byte-identical in every one, because none of these touches
the allocation that fails:

| attempt | free at failure | requested |
|---|---|---|
| `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.90` | 2.25 GiB | 2.37 GiB |
| `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.95` | 2.25 GiB | 2.37 GiB |
| `0.95 --enforce-eager` | 2.25 GiB | 2.37 GiB |
| `0.95` + speculative `max_model_len: 2048` | 2.25 GiB | 2.37 GiB |
| `0.95` + speculative `quantization: compressed-tensors` | 2.25 GiB | 2.37 GiB |
| `0.95` + **PR #49553 applied locally** | 2.25 GiB | 2.37 GiB |

`gpu_memory_utilization` sizes the KV pool, `enforce_eager` controls graph capture, and
`max_model_len` sizes the draft context -- all of them after the weights load. The error is
`Failed to load model`.

The decoder layers are **not** falling back to unquantized; the log carries
`[compressed_tensors_wNa16.py:137] Using MarlinLinearKernel for CompressedTensorsWNA16`.

#### Why this is not #49552 / #49553

[#49552](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/49552) and its fix
[#49553](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49553) describe MTP decoder layers silently
resolving to Unquantized because INC/AutoRound `block_name_to_quantize` prefixes are not mapped
from HF names to vLLM names for the draft. That is a different path: this checkpoint is
compressed-tensors, its MTP decoder layers quantize correctly, and the failing allocation is an
embedding, which is never quantized either way.

I applied #49553's one-line change to my install and re-ran: the OOM is unchanged. Tested rather
than assumed, since the symptoms are adjacent.

I also searched open issues and PRs for MTP plus memory. The 15 results are all a different
failure -- KV-cache **over**-allocation from a negative CUDA-graph estimate
([#44740](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/44740) and relatives), whose workaround is
to *lower* utilization. Nothing there is a load-time OOM on the draft.

#### What a fix might look like

I have not sent a patch because I am not sure which is wanted, and both touch shared code:

1. Alias the draft's `embed_tokens` to the target's when the draft has no embedding of its own in
   the checkpoint, the way `lm_head` is aliased under `tie_word_embeddings`.
2. Do not construct `VocabParallelEmbedding` in the MTP module at all when the checkpoint carries
   no `mtp.embed_tokens`, and let the loader point at the target's.

Either would return 2.37 GiB on this configuration, which is more than the KV cache the baseline
arm ends up with (1.38 GiB). Happy to test a patch on this hardware.

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the
      bottom right corner of the documentation page, which can answer lots of frequently asked
      questions.

items.title: [Bug] SimpleCPUOffloadConnector (eager, TP=2, nightly dev1214): engine wedges at Running:0 / Waiting:3 (1 capacity + 2 deferred) — independent data point for the #45406 stranding family, with py-spy stacks from the wedged state
items.body:
### Summary

Reproduced the exact wedge family described in #45406's second trigger (FCFS + async KV-load parked requests stranded behind an unschedulable queue head), but with `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` (eager mode, CPU backend) on a recent nightly — providing an independent production data point with py-spy stacks and live `/metrics` from the wedged state.

### Environment

- vLLM: `0.26.1rc1.dev1214+gf6130145c` (nightly wheel, 2026-08-26)
- Hardware: 2× RTX 3090, TP=2, 128 GB host RAM, Ubuntu 22.04
- Model: hybrid linear-attention/full-attention 27B (GDN-style, 64 layers, `full_attention_interval=4`), fp8 KV cache, `block_size=1648`
- Server flags (relevant): `--kv-offloading-size 60 --kv-offloading-backend native` (→ `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` via `VLLM_USE_SIMPLE_KV_OFFLOAD=1`, eager mode), `--max-num-seqs 6`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096`, `--enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill`, MTP-style speculative decoding (dflash, 7 tokens), `VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL=1648`
- Load: sustained agentic traffic (~270 requests/hour, short-to-medium prompts, heavy prefix reuse — external prefix cache hit rate 84.7% right before the wedge)

**Local patch disclosure:** we carry three small local patches to `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py` (store-side hash registration — the fix for our own report #53498 — plus a final-flush-on-request-finish). None of them touch the load path, the scheduler, or the promotion logic. Notably, the hash-registration patch *enables* CPU-cache lookups that always miss on stock main (#53498), which is what makes the async-load path (`get_num_new_matched_tokens` → `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`) reachable in the first place on this connector. The stranding mechanism itself is scheduler-side and reachable with other connectors on stock main per #45406's FCFS reproduction with `OffloadingConnector`.

### Symptom

Engine wedged silently at 17:51 local time: no ERROR/WARNING lines, `/metrics` still served, `/health` green. Live metrics from the wedged state:

```
vllm:num_requests_running{...} 0.0
vllm:num_requests_waiting{...} 3.0
vllm:num_requests_waiting_by_reason{...,reason="capacity"} 1.0
vllm:num_requests_waiting_by_reason{...,reason="deferred"} 2.0
```

`Running: 0, Waiting: 3 (1 capacity + 2 deferred)` — the deferred pair matches `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`-style parked async loads (they had just matched CPU-resident prefix blocks), the capacity request is the unschedulable head. GPU KV usage was high (~80%+) right before the collapse after a burst of long-prompt requests.

py-spy on EngineCore main thread, two samples 10 s apart (engine alive, not deadlocked on a lock — busy-looping):

```
Thread 153859 (active): "MainThread"
    _process_engine_step (vllm/v1/engine/core.py:1477)   # the `time.sleep(0.001)` yield branch
    run_busy_loop (vllm/v1/engine/core.py:1413)
    run_engine_core (vllm/v1/engine/core.py:1354)
```

i.e. `step_fn()` keeps returning `model_executed=False` while `scheduler.has_requests()` is true — `schedule()` produces nothing schedulable every step, forever. Workers spin in `shm_broadcast.acquire_read`. Only a restart recovers; after restart with identical config and continued traffic the engine is healthy again.

### Analysis

Same structural pattern as #45388/#45406: the waiting-queue traversal hits the capacity-blocked head and `break`s; the two parked async-KV-load requests behind it are never reached by `_try_promote_blocked_waiting_request()`, so their `finished_recving`/load-completion signals are never consumed; nothing is running, so no blocks are ever freed; `schedule()` returns an empty step indefinitely while the engine reports healthy. #44560's admission gate doesn't cover this because the load requests were already admitted and re-queued via `skipped_waiting` when the async load was issued.

We did not capture `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG` in the incident window (production); the py-spy dumps and metric snapshots above were captured live during the wedge and are available in full if useful.

### Suggested direction

Merge #45406 (defense-in-depth skip-past-unschedulable-head when `self.running` is empty), and consider a watchdog: if `num_requests_running == 0` while `num_requests_waiting > 0` with `reason="deferred"` persists for N seconds, log at WARNING/ERROR (and/or expose it in `/health`) — a healthy-idle engine has waiting=0; this combination is always a wedge.

### Related

- #45406 — the fix PR (not merged); its second FCFS trigger is this exact mechanism
- #45388 / #42371 — original symptom family
- #44560 — admission-gate fix that this path bypasses (post-admission re-queue)
- #53498 — our prior report on SimpleCPUOffloadConnector hash registration (whose fix unmasks this path on this connector)

- [x] Searched existing issues (this is a data-point report supporting an existing open PR, not a duplicate bug report)
